title: O Come, O Come, Emmanuel
description: The Advent hymn to the tune Veni Emmanuel, in John Mason Neale's English words as Hymns Ancient and Modern printed them, with W. H. Monk's four parts arranged for 2 to 4 singers. Three verses, each with the refrain "Rejoice! Rejoice! Emmanuel", in E minor at a steady, unhurried pace; the tune moves mostly by step, with a few notes to a syllable on "Emmanuel" and "Israel".

credits.words: John Mason Neale (1851), as altered for Hymns Ancient and Modern (1861)
credits.tune: "Veni Emmanuel", from the Hymnal Noted (musical editor Thomas Helmore)
credits.arrangement: W. H. Monk's four parts (1861), adapted by Stackapella

licence.words: public domain: John Mason Neale's translation of "Veni, veni, Emmanuel" (Neale died 1866), beginning "Draw nigh, draw nigh, Emmanuel" in the Hymnal Noted and altered by the compilers of Hymns Ancient and Modern (their chairman Henry Williams Baker died 1877); verses 1 to 3 of the five, as printed in the Revised Edition, "Thee" capitalised in verse 3's refrain as printed there; "victory" sung in two syllables, as the Hymnal Noted prints "vict'ry"
licence.tune: public domain: the melody headed "From a French Missal in the National Library, Lisbon" in the Hymnal Noted (its musical editor Thomas Helmore died 1890), as Hymns Ancient and Modern prints it under the musical editorship of William Henry Monk (died 1889)
licence.arrangement: W. H. Monk's four parts for Hymns Ancient and Modern, No. 36 (1861), signed in that book's Index of Tunes, "Harmonized or Arranged by W. H. Monk" (Monk died 1889; public domain): Monk's chords in his key, fitted to the Revised Edition's tune (the refrain's "el" held three beats, where his 1861 tune has one, the parts holding his G chord), with the lower parts revoiced for 2 to 4 beginners. The alto takes each chord's third where Monk's alto doubles the tune or sits a fourth or a second under it: B3 under the G4 that ends lines 1 and 4 and the refrain's first half (his unison G4), approached from C4, the seventh of the D7 before it (his F#4); G#3 under the E4 that ends line 2 and the refrain (his B3); D4 under the second "O" and under "Em-" (his B3 and G4); C4, then D4, under "man-" and "God" (his held G4 a second under the tune's A4). At "here" (beat 33 of each verse) the alto crosses a third above the tune's held low D4, F#4 approached by step, where Monk doubles the D4, and the tenor takes the fifth, A3. The harmony parts hold one chord through the tune's slur on "Is-" (Monk moves his bass) and move with the tune only where one chord cannot carry its slurred notes ("man-", "God" and "ex-", where Monk changes chord too). The refrain's "Emmanuel" takes line 1's parts (Monk sets it over a D pedal: D3, C3, D3, D3). Monk's tenor, which lies above our alto under "man-" and "God" (his E4 and D4), is rewritten around G3, F#3, A3 and B3. The bass keeps Monk's roots, with D#3 under "ly" (B7 in first inversion, his B2) so the leading tone rises in the bass; A2 held under "man-" (his C3 and A2) and C3 under "Is-"; G3 at the ends of lines 1 and 4 (his G2), so no line has two leaps of a fifth; and G2, B2 or D3 at beats 16, 20, 38 and 40 of each verse, where his note would move in octaves or fifths with the revoiced parts. His crotchet passing notes under "That" become one note. The last chord is his E major (the Revised Edition ends in E minor), with the tenor and bass in unison on E3 so the alto can take G# under the tune; it has no fifth. Breaths written in for beginners: each line's last note gives up its last beat. The tenor sings E3, not A3, on "That", "From" and "Dis-" at the start of each verse's third line, so it doesn't leap E to A in octaves with the tune across the breath (the choral review).
licence.source: Hymns Ancient and Modern for use in the Services of the Church, with Accompanying Tunes, compiled and arranged under the musical editorship of William Henry Monk (London: printed for the proprietors by William Clowes and Sons), the Revised Edition (473 hymns; Julian's Dictionary of Hymnology dates the new edition 1875), No. 49, "O come, O come, Emmanuel", pp. 34 and 35, "To be sung in Unison", in E minor (one sharp), barred in four minims and written here in crotchets (4/4), in its printed key; the tune and the words read from the Harold B. Lee Library copy (catalogued 1874, New York: Pott, Young & Co.) at archive.org/details/hymnsancientmode00monk/page/n49 and n50, and checked against the London printing catalogued 1890 at archive.org/details/hymnsancientmode0000unse_s2j4/page/n50; the harmony from the first edition with tunes (London: Novello and Co., preface dated Lent 1861), No. 36, in E minor, read from the University of Toronto copy at archive.org/details/hymnsancientmode00unse/page/n65 (words on n66; its Index of Tunes, n23, gives the tune "From French Missal, at Lisbon" and its harmony to W.
